To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
instructions can facilitate the transfer of ordinal information through equivalence relations.
the transfer of ordinal relations across equivalence classes was facilitated by the addition of instructions that reviewed the equivalence classes and sequence relations.

(1) the transfer of ordinal relations across equivalence classes can be demonstrated with adult humans, (2) this transfer can be accomplished with minimal instructions, and (3) it can be achieved more easily when the subjects are taught a sequence composed of stimuli that belong to the same equivalence classes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
instructions can be useful in promoting equivalence class formation and in promoting transfer of trained ordinal functions through equivalence relations.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of instructions in transfer of ordinal functions has been overstated.

, in the context of the present experiments, instructions about the match- to-sample and sequence tasks were critical to the formation of equivalence classes and to the transfer of trained ordinal functions through those classes.

instructions can be important for the transfer of functions through equivalence classes, and the role of instructions may vary depending on the specific experimental design and the specific instructions provided.
